Annapurna: First Conquest of an 8000-meter Peak (1951) is a book by French climber Maurice Herzog , leader of the 1950 French Annapurna expedition , the first expedition in history to summit and return from an 8000+ meter mountain, Annapurna in the Himalayas . It is considered a classic of mountaineering literature and perhaps the most influential climbing book ever written.

Description:

This famous work is an account of the French 1950 expedition to climb the Himalayan mountain Annapurna the 10th-highest mountain in the world. Maurice Herzog’s (1919- 2012) account of the expedition was first published in French 1951, and in English in 1952.

Condition

Vg. From the library of Keith Hyatt (1932-2021), acarologist at the Natural History Museum, London, and member the Museum expedition to Nepal during the 1950s, with his signature to endpaper.
